violation_type.title: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended (26 TAC §744.3805(4))
violation_type.short_title: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended
violation_type.typical_finding: Based on evidence obtained during the DFPS investigation, there is sufficient evidence to support a five year old child was left on the van for approximately 90 minutes unattended.

finding_variants.text: Based on evidence obtained during the DFPS investigation, there is sufficient evidence to support a five year old child was left on the van for approximately 90 minutes unattended.

During the course of a DFPS investigation, it was determined that caregivers failed to account for all children, resulting in a child being left on the bus alone. The vehicle was returned to another operation location, where the child was left on the bus for approximately 15 minutes.  Staff were unaware of the child's absence from the group until the child's parent came to pick them up from care.

Based on the information obtained during the DFPS investigation, the caregiver failed to follow the operation's transportation procedures by checking the van for any children or belongings resulting in the child being left in the vehicle for approx. 1.5 hours.

Based on the information obtained during the DFPS investigation, the caregiver failed to follow the operation's transportation procedures by checking the van for any children or belongings resulting in the child being left in the vehicle for over 2 hours.
Children were observed unattended in the daycare van while parked in front of the gas station.
Based on information obtained during an investigation, it was found that a child was left unattended on a transportation vehicle.
